correctness.rationale: Hom vertices are indexed length-m closed walks. Cyclic backtrack cancellation contracts any backtracking walk in |H|; under girth>=m−1 any shorter nonbacktracking closed walk cannot have a nontrivial cycle. A cyclic nonbacktracking length-m walk with repeated vertex would contain a forbidden shorter simple cycle; therefore it is an oriented based embedding of a simple m-cycle, exactly 2m for each unoriented cycle. Such an embedding is a zero-cell isolated from every one-coordinate change, because two distinct common neighbors of its adjacent image vertices would form a four-cycle, excluded by girth>=5. Matsushita Theorem 5.8 and Lemma 5.11 provide null-image components and their homotopy equivalent H / connected double-cover types, yielding |H×K2|. Each embedded m-cycle generates a free D_m orbit, while the null components form one component orbit; subtracting trivial H0 gives c_m invariant rank. Independent direct enumeration on C5,C6,C7,C8 as targets verified isolated counts 0,12,0,16 respectively for sources m6,m6,m8,m8; not a proof for all graphs. Sharpness via H=C_{m−2} for even m>=8 holds because length m closed walk with one inserted backtrack carries nontrivial winding not covered by m-simple traversals.

originality.rationale: Matsushita and Fujii–Kimura–Nozaki classify square-free-target Hom connected-component homotopy types, and cycle-to-cycle work gives special winding components. The target-specific high-girth rigidity turns all non-null components into a number of exactly counted isolated traversals, identifies their free dihedral actions and the integral component module, and obtains rational cycle detection for arbitrary high-girth H. These exact combinatorial/equivariant outputs were not already stated by the inspected broader structural theorem; they are a substantive specialization, with a possible derived-corollary priority risk acknowledged.

value.rationale: Cycle detection from equivariant reduced degree-zero homology is a natural exact graph invariant, not merely a component count of one small graph. The all-target high-girth rigidity bound is sharp and promotes a general Hom-component classification to explicit orbit and integral module structure; this is a meaningful structural lemma for graph Hom complexes.

final_claim: For every even m>=6 and connected loopless finite graph H with at least one edge and girth at least m-1, Hom(C_m,H) is homotopy equivalent to |H×K_2| plus exactly 2m c_m(H) isolated points, one free regular D_m orbit per unoriented simple m-cycle, and dimension of the D_m-invariant reduced rational H_0 equals c_m(H).
limitations: Girth at least m−1 and even m≥6 necessary to use this exact argument.
The homotopy equivalence is not claimed equivariant; action is on components/integral H0 lattice only.
